statements.quote: We anticipate our full year 2025 capital expenditures will be in the range of $60-65 billion.
statements.notes: This is total capex, not AI capex. The AI link is in the next sentence: growth is driven by generative AI and the core business. Elsewhere management says the majority of 2025 capex goes to the core business.

statements.quote: These are all big investments -- especially the hundreds of billions of dollars that we will invest in AI infrastructure over the long term.
statements.notes: 'Hundreds of billions' is a vague magnitude, not a stated amount or range, so it is recorded as qualitative. The horizon is 'over the long term', which is multi-year and not just the year after fiscal 2024.

statements.quote: And then in terms of the breakdown for core versus Gen AI use cases, we’re expecting total infrastructure spend within each of Gen AI, non-AI and core AI to increase in ‘25 with the majority of our CapEx directed to our core business with some caveat that that is -- that’s not easy to measure perfectly as the data centers we’re building can support AI or non-AI workloads and the GPU- based servers we procure for gen AI can be repurposed for core AI use cases and so on and so forth.
statements.notes: Says Gen AI and core AI infrastructure spend will increase, but gives no figure. The 'majority' refers to the core business, which includes both core AI and non-AI, so it is not an AI share.

statements.quote: We are planning to significantly ramp up deployment of GPUs in 2025, and we’ll continue to engage with our vendors and invest in our own silicon to meet those needs.

On the data center side, we’re anticipating higher data center spend in 2025 to be driven by build-outs of our large training clusters and our higher power density data centers that are entering the core construction phase.
statements.notes: The AI link is implicit ('large training clusters'). The next sentence says the capacity serves core AI and non-AI use cases.

statements.quote: And here, growth in employee comp and headcount more broadly is primarily driven by those areas that I mentioned, infrastructure monetization, generative AI, Reality Labs, and regulation and compliance.
statements.notes: Generative AI is one of several named drivers of 2025 employee compensation growth. The year comes from the preceding sentence in the same passage, which names 2025.

statements.quote: In 2025, we expect headcount growth will continue to be primarily driven by technical roles across our priority initiatives within infrastructure, monetization, Reality Labs, generative AI, as well as regulation and compliance.
statements.notes: This covers headcount growth, a proxy for opex. Generative AI is one of several drivers.

none_found.reason: Meta is a buyer of AI infrastructure. No sentence states an AI revenue amount or share. p02 only says AI initiatives aim to increase revenue growth.
